text: Anthropic jumped 17% in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday in a seminal moment for artificial intelligence, after the company completed the biggest initial public offering on record, topping SpaceX' s historic debut in June. The stock closed at $97.17 per share. The Claude creator, trading under the ticker "ANT," opened at $111.50, after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. At Thursday's close, Anthropic had a fully diluted market cap of roughly $1.8 trillion. More than 846 million shares changed hands, surpassing the 522 million shares that were traded on SpaceX's opening day. The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. Anthropic closed with a market capitalization of roughly $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis, behind just Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX on the list of the most-valuable U.S. companies. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic investors Amazon and Google own roughly 28% of the company's outstanding capital stock following the offering. The company said Amazon owns 14.7%, while Google owns 13.7%, according to its prospectus. Google initially invested in Anthropic in late 2022, not long before the company first launched its Claude chatbot in 2023. Amazon announced its initial investment in Anthropic in September of 2023. Anthropic is also a major customer of both companies. — Ashley Capoot Protestors are gathered outside Anthropic's offices in San Francisco following the company's Nasdaq debut. More than 100 people are there and chanting, "ban AI that builds AI," and passing cars are honking in support. Jacob Coxon , the former Anthropic researcher who raised early concerns about the potentially dire risks of AI, said he plans to speak at the demonstration, according to a post on X . He shared a link to a website called "Ban RSI," which reads, "Their IPO. Our Lives." Coxon and other industry researchers have grown worried about recursive self-improvement , or RSI, which means that an AI system is capable of designing and developing its successor without human intervention. RSI is not yet possible, but companies, including Anthropic, have warned that it would make it easier for humans to lose control over those systems. "Anthropic uses AI to build better AI," the Ban RSI website says. "They are making trillions doing so. Recursive self-improvement puts humanity in danger. This needs to stop. Ban RSI." — Ashley Capoot Thursday was Anthropic's day, and offered Wall Street a much-needed break from Nvidia news. Nvidia, a major Anthropic investor and partner, has been roiled by scandal in recent weeks. Jensen Huang , who co-founded the chipmaker 33 years ago, resigned as CEO following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker agreed to purchase roughly $10 billion worth of Anthropic's Class N common stock as part of a private placement that took place immediately following the completion of the offering. Nvidia previously agreed to invest up to $10 billion in the company in November of last year. — Ashley Capoot AMD CEO Lisa Su congratulated Anthropic in a post on X . "Congratulations @DarioAmodei, @DanielaAmodei, @NotTomBrown and the whole @AnthropicAI team on an incredible milestone! Proud to be your partner," Su wrote. Shares of AMD are down roughly 8% after a short seller alleged the company's firmware repeatedly appeared at a blacklisted Chinese company and related entities. AMD is an Anthropic investor and participated in the company's private placement. It's also a chip supplier to Anthropic. — Ashley Capoot Investors may be cheering Anthropic's blockbuster trading debut, but some Democratic lawmakers see the mammoth IPO as one more reason to demand regulations on the AI industry. "A record-breaking IPO for a company worth $1.5 trillion… and still NO action on AI regulation," said Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., the vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, in an X post. "We cannot wait any longer. We must pass my legislation to get some guardrails around this tech," said Warner, referring to legislation unveiled Thursday that would require disclosures from publicly traded companies on AI-related financing. "I'm alarmed that Anthropic is barreling ahead with its IPO today despite a series of outages in critically important systems," Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said on X. "Wall Street shouldn't be cashing in on a company that could turn out to be a ticking time bomb or a Trojan horse for hackers and foreign adversaries. Going public cements a broken business model and rewards its reckless pace," Jayapal wrote. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who is running to be the next Senate majority leader, said on Wednesday, "The last 24 hours and the next 24 hours show us how urgent it is to address the risks posed by AI." That IPO "will be great for the billionaires, but we need to act urgently to address the threats to the rest of us," Van Hollen said in a social media video . — Kevin Breuninger Anthropic became the 10th publicly traded U.S. tech company currently valued at $1 trillion or more. The group had been bigger until AMD and Micron suffered slumps that pushed them out of the four-comma club. OpenAI, meanwhile, is still private. Here are the other members and their market caps as of Wednesday's close: — Ari Levy Trading volume in Anthropic on its first day on the Nasdaq has already surpassed the number of SpaceX shares that were traded in its debut. As of mid-day, more than 640 million Anthropic shares had changed hands. On SpaceX's opening day in June, a total of 522 million shares were traded. Anthropic is also the most actively traded stock on the Nasdaq. — Samantha Subin Anthropic has made headlines in recent months for its advanced artificial intelligence models with sophisticated cybersecurity capabilities. In a bid to curb bad actors from exploiting them, the AI lab then limited access to select customers through Project Glasswing. Anthropic has since broadened the pool of testers and launched a cybersecurity initiative aimed at protecting critical infrastructure. But these moves have raised questions over whether the company will scale its cybersecurity business — or even pit it against major security vendors, including partners. Cybersecurity could match Anthropic's coding opportunity and reach $500 billion annually, Wolfe Research analysts wrote in a Thursday note. "Act 2 is Cyber which given the last week seems like it could be as big as Coding," they wrote. That market might include AI security operations, patching or penetration testing — simulated cyberattacks utilized to identity a company's security weaknesses. "We think that model providers will offer a solution to replace the security team that is manually analyzing data with agents who can respond at machine speed," they added. — Samantha Subin Wall Street banks are set to reap a huge windfall from Anthropic's IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley among the biggest earners. The company disclosed in its latest SEC filing that it agreed to pay the banks $550 million, surpassing the roughly $500 million payday banks took in from SpaceX's IPO in June. — Annie Palmer Anthropic's investors and other partners are taking a victory lap upon the AI lab's successful debut. Investors Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed dedicated the front page of their websites to congratulating Anthropic, as did counsel Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati . Bessemer's Byron Deeter posted a thread on X detailing the backstory of the firm's investment in Anthropic. — Caleigh Keating Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy, an early Anthropic investor, said the firm's aggregate position in the AI company is around $25 billion. "Clearly the most epic return for Menlo Ventures in our history, and one of the top handful in the history of venture capital," Murphy told CNBC in an interview. "We feel grateful. We have over five LPs that we've delivered over a billion dollars of returns to, and at the end of the day, that's really our job." — Ashley Capoot Ashton Kutcher congratulated Dario Amodei and "the whole team at Anthropic" in a post on X shortly before the AI company's first trade. Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures , a Los Angeles-based venture capital firm, which invested in Anthropic in 2023 and participated in several subsequent funding rounds. The VC firm also counts Guy Oseary, the legendary talent manager for musicians including Madonna, among its cofounders. Bloomberg reported that Sound Ventures owns roughly half a percent of Anthropic, citing sources familiar with the matter. Sound Ventures' stake is likely now worth billions of dollars after the company's lofty IPO. — Annie Palmer Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, called Anthropic 's IPO a " Google moment" for the frontier lab during CNBC's Halftime Report. At over $2 trillion in market capitalization, Anthropic has entered Google's ranks as one of the most valuable companies in the world, behind Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon . But Deeter says Anthropic doesn't need to "dominate intelligence" in the same way that Google dominates search. The artificial intelligence ecosystem will see "multiple great businesses," Deeter says, adding that he expects Anthropic to continue to be a market leader while also pacing the frontier of AI model development. — Isabel O'Brien Anthropic has an unusual governance structure . The company is a public benefit corporation, which means it's required to balance the financial interest of stockholders, the best interests of those affected by its conduct and its "company purpose." Anthropic said in its prospectus that its purpose is to facilitate the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity." Anthropic's seven co-founders also wield a lot of power over the company. Prior to the completion of its offering, Anthropic issued a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company called "Founder LLC." Anthropic's co-founders are the sole members of Founder LLC, and the entity holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. Each co-founder sold 3.38 million shares in the IPO, according to the prospectus, for total proceeds of $1.96 billion. Additionally, Anthropic introduced an independent governance body called the " Long-Term Benefit Trust " in 2023, which has the authority to elect and remove the majority of the company's board of directors. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic opened with a market capitalization of nearly $2.01 trillion, behind only Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet and Amazon . — Ashley Capoot Ben Bernanke, the former chair of the Federal Reserve , is in the room at the Nasdaq as investors celebrate Anthropic's first trade. Anthropic in July appointed Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the AI company's independent governance structure that advises it and appoints its board members. — Annie Palmer Anthropic shares popped 34% in the company's Nasdaq debut. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic is indicated to open at $111 per share, a person familiar told CNBC. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic is indicated to open at $110 a share, a person familiar told CNBC. — Ashley Capoot Amodei told JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon in a fireside chat on Friday that he thinks talent and culture are the "most important things" that drive a company's success, which is why he and his co-founders have tried to place so much emphasis on those areas at Anthropic. Anthropic requires every employee to pass a culture interview, which is taken very seriously, Amodei said. He added that he spends roughly half of his time focusing on talent and culture at the company. "We've been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented, but who don't fit our culture," Amodei said. "We don't want people who are jerks. We don't want people who try to steal the show and don't work well with others. We don't want people who aren't oriented towards the public benefit." Amodei also regularly holds DVQs, which stands for "Dario Vision Quests," where he speaks in front of the entire company. He said he tries to update employees by talking honestly and avoiding "corpo speak." "It means that the leaders of the company can trust the employees," Amodei said. "The employees of the company can trust the leaders of the company to be candid. Everyone feels that we're being honest with them, and that has this enormous value." — Ashley Capoot Ben Reitzes, head of technology research at Melius, said growth and leverage as well as efficiency gains outweigh margin concerns when it comes to estimating Anthropic's future growth path. "They're ahead of the game in models, making them more efficient, and their cost to train is going down, and the speed to train is going down. So they're going to be putting out models at such a rapid clip that are on the frontier," Reitzes told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "That makes them more valuable and worth paying for." Melius initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and price target of $155 per share. Reitzes said Melius compared Anthropic to hyperscalers and said its assigned value could even be "conservative." "The reason it's conservative is much better growth, and the leverage here could be insane." — Caleigh Keating Anthropic prioritized allocating shares to institutional investors it had relationships with, according to people familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That meant roughly half of the firms that placed orders were left empty-handed, they said. It's normal in most IPOs for some portion of institutional investors not to receive any allocation, but that was a higher number than usual for this offering, one person said. Anthropic's management team had experience working with institutional investors from raising capital through private rounds, so the company had a strong view of what would make up a good shareholder base construction, the person said. Retail allocation came in at around 15%, the people said. Anthropic had estimated that about 20% of the offering would go to retail, as CNBC previously reported, a higher percentage than the typical 5% to 10% allotment. — Leslie Picker and Ashley Capoot Protestors are gathering outside of the Nasdaq ahead of the listing. The New York City Democratic Socialists of America shared a post on Instagram on Wednesday encouraging demonstrators to attend a rally at 9 a.m. ET on Thursday. The group said Anthropic "is driving the AI bubble to get rich quick before the bubble bursts." "Join our rally to send a message to all Big Tech oligarchs and demand a freeze to reckless AI development and destruction," the group said. Other organizations, including Climate Defiance, Act Up and New York Communities for Change are also sponsoring the protest. — Ashley Capoot As with SpaceX's offering, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led Anthropic's IPO. Some 20 other banks are listed on the prospectus, including JPMorgan Chase , Citigroup and Barclays . — Ari Levy Retail investors with access to the Anthropic IPO who try to sell the stock for a quick profit may face a penalty from their brokerage . Anthropic made shares available to retail investors through brokerages including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E-Trade and some of their respective affiliates, the AI startup said in an IPO prospectus. Many of them have "anti-flipping" policies meant to discourage investors who purchase IPO shares from dumping them fast. These policies apply only to retail investors who place an order with their brokerage firm to buy the Anthropic IPO at its offering price — something many investors don't have access to. For example, Fidelity clients who sell IPO shares within the first 15 calendar days from the start of trading in the secondary market would be barred from participating in future stock IPOs through the brokerage. Investors get a six-month ban after the first offense and could be permanently barred after the third offense. — Greg Iacurci Anthropic is indicated to open at $105 a share, representing a nearly 27% jump from its $83 IPO price. A source familiar with the matter told CNBC that the stock is expected to open this hour. — Samantha Subin Anthropic has had two major disputes with the Trump administration this year, but tensions have begun to thaw between the two camps in recent months. Amodei joined Trump for a private dinner at the White House in September, which marked the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders. Days later, Amodei attended a luncheon at the White House, where he signed a voluntary AI safety accord. Three months earlier, the company had to temporarily disable access to two of its most advanced models, Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, in order to comply with an export control directive from the government that cited "national security authorities." Anthropic restored the models after roughly two weeks of tense negotiations. In March, Anthropic was banned by the Pentagon after discussions about how the military could use its AI models spiraled out of control. The company sued the Trump administration to try to reverse the blacklisting. — Ashley Capoot Retail investors who don't want to buy Anthropic stock directly will get access to the AI startup courtesy of many popular mutual funds and exchange-traded funds . Index funds won't add Anthropic stock immediately. Some will add them within days or weeks, depending on the inclusion rules of specific indexes. For example, the Morningstar U.S. Total Market Index will add the stock after five trading days. The Nasdaq-100 will add it after Dec. 18. The S&P 500 won't add it for at least a year. Many actively managed funds held pre-IPO Anthropic shares — and investors in those funds automatically get a sliver of Anthropic's IPO when it starts trading. A handful of the most heavily concentrated funds held pre-IPO shares worth more than 10% of their overall portfolios. Most investors' exposure to Anthropic in mutual funds and ETFs will likely be relatively low — well below 1% of the overall portfolio for most funds, experts said. — Greg Iacurci Daniela Amodei said she and Dario are "so proud" of the Anthropic team. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety." — Caleigh Keating The pressure is on Anthropic over the expectations tied to being the largest IPO on record. "We've been calm about it," CEO Dario Amodei said. Despite the turn in the spotlight, Amodei said the company is laser-focused on the fundamentals. "We always want to under promise and over deliver," he said. "You know, that's our core." — Samantha Subin Daniela Amodei said the company is focusing on listening to consumers when it comes to data centers in the wake of the midterms. "One of the things that I think is really important to Anthropic is for it to feel to people like this technology is not happening to them. And I think really from our perspective, building data centers is something where we also need to listen to what it is that those communities want and help to bring forward that future as well." — Caleigh Keating Daniela Amodei said Anthropic is a "long-term focused company," so it thinks about its debut as just one step along its journey. "While today is a super exciting milestone, and we're obviously really, really excited about it, I think it's, for us, it's like one stop on the journey," she said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'" — Ashley Capoot Anthropic President Daniela Amodei touted the company's public benefit structure. "We're really trying to do something that we do think can have this incredible economic value and impact, but we want it to be baked into essentially our structure," she said. — Samantha Subin Dario Amodei said the balance between growth and pacing was one of the "central tensions" at the heart of Anthropic. "What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way." — Caleigh Keating Dario Amodei said while the scaling laws behind AI suggested the technology would become extremely capable, even he has been surprised to see it play out. "And it's happening right now." — Ashley Capoot Anthropic said its underwriters have the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares of Class A common stock from the company, according to a Thursday filing , which would net the company another $12.2 billion. Assuming that option is exercised, Anthropic would raise a total of $93.5 billion through its IPO, topping the $85.7 billion raised by SpaceX. Anthropic's underwriters have until Nov. 20 to exercise the option. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic executives were sporting "Clawd" pins while they rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq. "I think this level of demand for the company from Altimeter and others, and from retail investors getting in the game, getting their shot on goal the first time, is real evidence of just how extraordinary this company has operated," Gerstner told CNBC's "Squawk Box." Gerstner's Altimeter Capital is planning on investing $5 billion in the AI lab, which he called a "cornerstone" investment for his firm. "This isn't a get-rich-quick scheme. As I've said, this will be a cornerstone investment for Altimeter. This is a multi-year compounder in the most important super cycle in the history of technology," Gerstner told CNBC. — Caleigh Keating Amodei is speaking about AI's potential benefits and risks in his address at the Nasdaq. "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," Amodei said. "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same." — Ashley Capoot Daniela Amodei spoke from the Nasdaq ahead of the opening bell, and had a message for people who are scared of AI. "This technology needs you — not your trust, not your use, but your voice," she said. "The end of this story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us." —Chris Eudaily Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was larger than demand for any other deal in history, sources told CNBC's David Faber. Anthropic targeted retail allocation of about 20%, as CNBC previously reported, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors. Anthropic's stock could trade into the low $100s on Thursday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. — Ashley Capoot The average Anthropic employee will be worth over $40 million after today's IPO, marking one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history. The AI lab has generated 1.77 billion employee options. Earlier hires stand to benefit even further, with over 400 employees expected to be worth $100 million or more at the current share price. Lockup periods may alter the timeline for the gains to make it to the economy, but the newfound wealth is expected to supercharge the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropic giving. — Robert Frank, Caleigh Keating As of around 8:00 a.m. ET, the scene outside the Nasdaq is pretty sleepy, though there is some police presence. The Nasdaq isn't promoting Anthropic's logo yet, but there are some ads for Elon Musk's Grok Bot and the neocloud Nebius . — Ashley Capoot Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei, have arrived at the Nasdaq in New York City. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic is headed for a big first-day pop, if trading in the perpetual futures market is any indication. The futures in Anthropic on the Hyperliquid exchange were trading above $104, indicating a surge of more than 25% from its $83 IPO price. Anthropic trading in so-called perp futures on Polymarket were also showing a jump to similar levels. "Early indications are that it's up about 25%," said J.J. Kinahan, senior VP of retail and alternative investments at CBOE Global Markets, on CNBC "Squawk Box." "With some of the tumultuous times here for Nvidia, a little bit of that trust has gone away from the retail investor so this is the way people I think are going to express themselves." Perpetual futures are a crypto-based new type of futures contract which never expire and don't represent any ownership in the companies its tracking. The derivatives correctly predicted the initial pop in the SpaceX IPO back in June. Retail investors are clamoring to buy Anthropic in the open market, according to Vanda Research. Retail net buying will be about $250 million, double that of SpaceX buying, the firm estimates. — John Melloy Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price, a sign of the importance of Anthropic's offering to the entire tech industry. — Ari Levy In June, SpaceX raised $75 billion in what was by far the largest IPO on record until Anthropic's share sale on Wednesday. Elon Musk's company ended up raising a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment. Anthropic is a major SpaceX customer, signing an agreement earlier this year "to spend an aggregate of up to $120.5 billion over terms extending into 2029, consisting of approximately $3.1 billion in the aggregate per month once all capacity has been delivered, which we expect in December 2026," according to the prospectus. — Ari Levy More than 90 academics and AI safety experts signed " The MisAnthropic Statement " ahead of the company's Nasdaq debut, blasting it for amassing power and rushing to build potentially dangerous technology. "Anthropic warns that recursively self-improving AI could concentrate power and escape human control, yet races to build it first," the statement says. "The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation. A representative for Anthropic declined to comment about the statement. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic's revenue has surged dramatically this year as more companies have adopted its AI models and products. The company said it generated roughly $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic's losses also widened, however. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, compared to a net loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. The vast majority of its loss, about $94.3 billion, comes from a change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, Anthropic said. The company said its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of the end of October, up roughly $10 billion from the previous month. — Ashley Capoot Anthropic said in its prospectus that it believes its seven co-founders are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission." The co-founders are the sole members of " Founder LLC ," a new entity that holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. The structure gives them "the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future," according to the filing.
